person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: In this paper we propose methods for estimating heterogeneity in causal effects in experimental and observational studies, and for conducting hypothesis tests about the magnitude of the differences in treatment effects across subsets of the population.

span.label: heterogeneous treatment effects
span.quote: In this paper we study two closely related problems: first, estimating heterogeneity by covariates or features in causal effects in experimental or observational studies, and second, conducting inference about the magnitude of the differences in treatment effects across subsets of the population.

span.label: simulation
span.quote: To assess the relative performance of the proposed algorithms we carried out a small simulation study with three distinct designs.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: honest estimation: use one sample to construct the tree partition and a separate sample to estimate treatment effects, removing overfitting bias
span.quote: one sample is used to construct the partition and another to estimate treatment effects for each subpopulation

span.label: requires the unconfoundedness (conditional randomization) assumption
span.quote: we maintain the assumption of randomization conditional on the covariates

span.label: Sample splitting for honest estimation costs precision, which is only partly offset by the removal of bias.
span.quote: Although there is a loss of precision due to sample splitting (which reduces sample size in each step of estimation), there is a benefit for fit in terms of eliminating bias that offsets at least part of the cost.

span.label: In the simulations honest estimation is measurably worse than adaptive estimation on treatment-effect mean-squared error.
span.quote: The results show that there is a cost to honest estimation in terms of MSEτ , varying by design and estimator.

span.label: The no-interference (SUTVA) assumption the methods rest on can fail when units are connected in a network.
span.quote: This assumption may be violated in settings where some units are connected through networks.

span.label: Hybrid variants (adaptive tree construction combined with honest leaf estimation) are left unexamined.
span.quote: We do not consider those variations in this paper.

span.label: The quantity the method estimates is never observed for any unit in the data.
span.quote: This creates complications for conventional methods because we do not observe unit level causal effects for any unit

span.label: The paper's central adjective is a stipulated property of data use, not a claim about candour.
span.quote: We say that a model is “honest” if it does not use the same information for selecting the model structure (in our case, the partition of the covariate space) and for estimation given a model structure

span.label: The improvement claimed for honesty is measured in coverage, and the paper names what it costs.
span.quote: we show that honest estimation can result in substantial improvements in coverage of confidence intervals, where our method attains nominal coverage rates, without much sacrifice in terms of fitting treatment effects

span.label: The comparison class is conventional tree estimation under a name the paper assigns it.
span.quote: We contrast ‘’honest” estimation with “adaptive” estimation used in conventional CART, where the same data is used to build the partition and estimate leaf effects

span.label: regression-tree (recursive partitioning) methods adapted to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects

span.label: 'honest' - A STIPULATED PROPERTY OF DATA USE: a model is honest when the information selecting its structure is not the information estimating its parameters, which is sample splitting and nothing about truthfulness, candour or good faith - all of which the word carries anyway
span.quote: We say that a model is “honest” if it does not use the same information for selecting the model structure (in our case, the partition of the covariate space) and for estimation given a model structure

span.label: 'adaptive' - THE NAME GIVEN TO THE ALTERNATIVE: conventional CART, where one sample does both jobs, is labelled adaptive here so that the two can be compared; the word is the paper's, applied to a practice that did not call itself that
span.quote: We contrast ‘’honest” estimation with “adaptive” estimation used in conventional CART, where the same data is used to build the partition and estimate leaf effects

span.label: the estimand - UNOBSERVABLE FOR EVERY UNIT: unit-level causal effects are not observed for any unit at all, so unlike an ordinary prediction problem there is no held-out truth anywhere in the data against which a per-unit estimate could be scored
span.quote: This creates complications for conventional methods because we do not observe unit level causal effects for any unit
